EXTREME PRESENCE
23 — 25 OCT. 2026

What can a museum
make present?

Museums organise attention. They give objects, practices, and ways of being a place in the world. What conditions let those worlds flourish?

Five rooms follow cultivation, devotion, memory, being, and interrelation. Change the definition below. See which possibilities remain.

THE MUSEUM SHOWS ITS WORK

Every list has
a point of view.

Loading sources…

01 / THE EXHIBITION

Nineteen selected cases connect museum forms to cultivation, devotion, memory, being, and interrelation. Institutional summaries link to their sources. Questions and thematic connections are editorial interpretations. Three hypothetical cases are explicitly labelled.

Illustrations are interpretive studies, not photographs of museum collections.

02 / THE ATLAS

Names, locations, and subject labels are extracted from publicly accessible museum lists. Records are merged by linked article or normalised name within a country. Each entry retains its contributing lists. Country and territory groupings follow those lists; they are not independently geocoded.

No description or opening status is invented for imported records. Blank fields remain unknown. Ambiguous table rows are excluded.

03 / THE LIMITS

This is a snapshot, not a census. English-language lists represent some places much more densely than others. Museums may have closed, moved, changed their names, or been misclassified. Some galleries, heritage sites, and collections appear because the source includes them.

The three definition switches apply only to the researched exhibition. Unknown is different from no.

04 / REUSE & CONTINUE

List-derived records are attributed to Wikipedia contributors and offered under CC BY-SA 4.0. Source pages preserve their edit histories. Raw source prose and photographs are not reproduced.
